name: Pellorneidae
description: Pellorneidae, the ground babblers, are a family of passerine birds found in tropical Asia and Africa. They are primarily terrestrial birds that forage on the forest floor, feeding on insects and other invertebrates.

children.name: Pellorneum
children.description: A genus of terrestrial babblers with streaked or spotted underparts, found in Asian forests.

children.name: Pellorneum ruficeps
children.description: The puff-throated babbler or spotted babbler (Pellorneum ruficeps) is a species of passerine bird found in Asia. They are found in scrub and moist forest mainly in hilly regions. They forage in small groups on the forest floor, turning around leaf litter to find their prey and usually staying low in the undergrowth where they can be hard to spot. However, they have loud and distinct calls, including a morning song, contact and alarm calls. It is the type species of the genus Pellorneum which may, however, currently include multiple lineages.

children.name: Pellorneum malaccense
children.description: The mourning babbler (Pellorneum malaccense), previously the short-tailed babbler, is a species of bird in the ground babbler family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Pellorneum rostratum
children.description:
The Malayan swamp babbler (Pellorneum rostratum), previously named the white-chested babbler, is a species of bird in the ground babbler family, Pellorneidae, that is found in the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, the Riau Islands, the Lingga Islands and the island of Belitung. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the Bornean swamp babbler (Pellorneum macropterum).
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Pellorneum tickelli
children.description: The buff-breasted babbler (Pellorneum tickelli) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Pellorneum pyrrogenys
children.description:
Temminck's babbler (Pellorneum pyrrogenys) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Borneo and Java. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
This bird's common name commemorates the Dutch naturalist Coenraad Jacob Temminck.

children.name: Pellorneum bicolor
children.description: The ferruginous babbler (Pellorneum bicolor) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Pellorneum palustre
children.description: The marsh babbler (Pellorneum palustre) is a member of the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Pellorneum nigrocapitatum
children.description: The Malayan black-capped babbler (Pellorneum nigrocapitatum) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found on the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Bangka Island, Belitung and North Natuna. This species, the Javan black-capped babbler (P. Capistratum) and the Bornean black-capped babbler (P. Capistratoides) were formerly considered conspecific, but were split from it in 2021. Together they were called the black-capped babbler. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Pellorneum cinereiceps
children.description: The ashy-headed babbler (Pellorneum cinereiceps) is a species of passerine bird in the ground babbler family Pellorneidae. The species is also known as the ashy-crowned babbler. The species is closely related to the short-tailed babbler. The two species are sometimes treated as the same species but differ in their calls. The species is monotypic, meaning it has no subspecies.

children.name: Pellorneum celebense
children.description: The Sulawesi babbler (Pellorneum celebense) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Pellorneum albiventre
children.description:
The spot-throated babbler (Pellorneum albiventre) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found mainly in Eastern Bangladesh, Bhutan, Northeast India, Yunnan, Myanmar and Vietnam.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Pellorneum capistratum
children.description: The Javan black-capped babbler (Pellorneum capistratum) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is endemic to the island of Java in Indonesia. The Malayan black-capped babbler (P. Nigrocapitatum) and the Bornean black-capped babbler (P. Capistratoides) were both formerly considered conspecific, but were split from it in 2021. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Pellorneum capistratoides
children.description: The Bornean black-capped babbler (Pellorneum capistratoides) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found on Borneo. This species, the Javan black-capped babbler (P. Capistratum) and the Malayan black-capped babbler (P. Nigrocapitatum) were formerly considered conspecific, but were split from it in 2021. Together they were called the black-capped babbler. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Pellorneum spiculifolium
children.description: This small ground babbler is found in the arid regions of sub-Saharan Africa, known for its distinctive calls and behavior that help it blend into its desert environment.

children.name: Malacocincla corynoides
children.description: This ground babbler species is found in the warm, dry regions of southern Asia and Australia, where it forages on leaf litter and seeds.

children.name: Malacopteron fulvum
children.description: This species has a distinctive orange and black coloration, with fluffy feathers on its head and neck. It is found in the high-altitude grasslands of South America.

children.name: Illadopsis fulvus
children.description: This small ground babbler species is characterized by its bright orange coloration, which helps it stand out against the surrounding foliage. It's found in the dense rainforests of South America.

children.name: Malacocincla notabilis
children.description: Endemic to the western parts of China, this species is known for its distinctive vocalizations and habitat preferences.

children.name: Napothera insignis
children.description: Found in the dense forests of Southeast Asia, this species is recognized by its bold plumage and shy nature.

children.name: Malacopteron melanocephala
children.description: A rare species, found in the mountainous regions of Vietnam and China, known for its striking black head and brown body.

children.name: Turdinus altipennis
children.description: Endemic to the high-altitude regions of Nepal and Bhutan, this species is well-adapted to cold climates.

children.name: Laticilla gracilis
children.description: Found in the grasslands of central China, this species is characterized by its slender build and unique plumage patterns.

children.name: Ptyrticus cineraceus
children.description: Known for its ashy plumage and preference for forest edges, this species is widespread in the Eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Graminicola fuliginosa
children.description: Found in the grasslands of northern India, this species is known for its rich brown coloration and ground-dwelling habits.

children.name: Malacocincla
children.description: A genus of medium-sized, plain-coloured ground babblers found in Southeast Asia.

children.name: Malacocincla abbotti
children.description: Abbott's babbler (Malacocincla abbotti) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is widely distributed along the Himalayas in South Asia and extending into the forests of Southeast Asia. They are short-tailed and stout birds which forage in pairs in dense undergrowth close to the ground and their presence is indicated by their distinctive calls.

children.name: Malacocincla sepiaria
children.description:
Horsfield's babbler (Malacocincla sepiaria) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
The common name commemorates the American naturalist Thomas Horsfield.

children.name: Malacocincla perspicillata
children.description: The black-browed babbler (Malacocincla perspicillata) is a songbird species in the family Pellorneidae. The species is endemic to Borneo. Only a single specimen collected in the nineteenth century was known, until the species was rediscovered in Borneo in 2020.

children.name: Napothera
children.description: A genus of small, short-tailed babblers that inhabit dense forest undergrowth in Asia.

children.name: Napothera epilepidota
children.description:
The eyebrowed wren-babbler (Napothera epilepidota) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its range extends from the eastern Himalayas throughout Southeast Asia.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Napothera brunnescens
children.description: A recently split wren-babbler from Java, formerly considered conspecific with N. crassa.

children.name: Napothera pasquieri
children.description:
The white-throated wren-babbler (Napothera pasquieri) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Napothera danjoui
children.description: The short-tailed scimitar babbler or Indochinese wren-babbler, (Napothera danjoui) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Laos and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest. It is threatened by habitat loss. The Naung Mung scimitar babbler was formerly considered a distinct species, but is now considered conspecific.

children.name: Malacopteron
children.description: A genus of medium-sized babblers with rufous or chestnut crowns, found in Southeast Asian forests.

children.name: Malacopteron cinereum
children.description: The scaly-crowned babbler (Malacopteron cinereum) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Malacopteron magnum
children.description: The rufous-crowned babbler (Malacopteron magnum) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, and Thailand. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Malacopteron affine
children.description:
The sooty-capped babbler (Malacopteron affine) is a member of the family Pellorneidae. It occurs in Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei, Thailand, and Singapore.
The sooty-capped babbler is also known in Malay as rimba tinjau belukar. Its main diet is small insects.

children.name: Malacopteron albogulare
children.description: The grey-breasted babbler (Malacopteron albogulare) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia and Malaysia. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical swampland. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Malacopteron magnirostre
children.description: The moustached babbler (Malacopteron magnirostre) is a species of bird in the ground babbler family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Kenopia
children.description: A monotypic genus of wren-babbler with striking black-and-white striped plumage, found in Southeast Asian forests.

children.name: Kenopia striata
children.description: The striped wren-babbler (Kenopia striata) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is monotypic within the genus Kenopia. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical swampland. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Turdinus
children.description: A genus of large wren-babblers with stout bills and thrush-like proportions, found in Southeast Asian forests.

children.name: Turdinus macrodactylus
children.description: The large wren-babbler (Turdinus macrodactylus) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra and Java. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Turdinus atrigularis
children.description:
The black-throated wren-babbler (Turdinus atrigularis) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is endemic to the island of Borneo (mainly southern Brunei and East Malaysia).
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest. It resides primarily in the understory. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Turdinus marmoratus
children.description: The marbled wren-babbler (Turdinus marmoratus) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in the Malay Peninsula and the Barisan Mountains of Sumatra. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Turdinus everetti
children.description: A wren-babbler endemic to the mountains of Borneo, with a rich chestnut back.

children.name: Gypsophila
children.description: A genus of wren-babblers adapted to limestone karst habitats in Southeast Asia.

children.name: Gypsophila crassa
children.description: The mountain wren-babbler (Gypsophila crassa) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is native to the Iran Mountains of northeastern Borneo. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Gypsophila crispifrons
children.description: The variable limestone babbler (Gypsophila crispifrons) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in the limestone hills of northern and eastern Thailand northwest to southern Myanmar. Two other Gypsophila species, the Annam limestone babbler (G. Annamensis) and the rufous limestone babbler (G. Calcicola) were previously considered subspecies of G. Crispifrons, but a 2020 study found them to be distinct species.

children.name: Gypsophila annamensis
children.description:
The Annam limestone babbler (Gypsophila annamensis), also known as the khướu đá hoa in Vietnamese, is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is native to the limestone hills of northern Indochina. It was formerly considered a subspecies of the variable limestone babbler (G. Crispifrons) but a 2020 study recovered it as a distinct species.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Gypsophila calcicola
children.description:
The rufous limestone babbler (Gypsophila calcicola) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is endemic to the limestone hills of central Thailand. It was formerly considered a subspecies of the variable limestone babbler (G. Crispifrons) but a 2020 study recovered it as a distinct species.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Laticilla
children.description: A genus of long-tailed, grassland-dwelling babblers found in South Asia.

children.name: Laticilla burnesii
children.description: The rufous-vented grass babbler or rufous-vented prinia (Laticilla burnesii) is a small warbler in the family Pellorneidae that occurs in Pakistan, northwestern India and Nepal.

children.name: Laticilla cinerascens
children.description: The swamp grass babbler or swamp prinia (Laticilla cinerascens) is a small bird of the Indian subcontinent. Some authorities consider it a subspecies of the rufous-vented grass babbler.

children.name: Illadopsis
children.description: A genus of African forest babblers, the only pellorneid genus found in Africa. They are secretive, thrush-like birds of the forest understorey.

children.name: Illadopsis fulvescens
children.description: The brown illadopsis (Illadopsis fulvescens) or brown thrush-babbler, is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Illadopsis rufipennis
children.description: The pale-breasted illadopsis (Illadopsis rufipennis) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found throughout the African tropical rainforest (including Bioko). The Tanzanian illadopsis was formerly considered a subspecies. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Illadopsis puveli
children.description: Puvel's illadopsis (Illadopsis puveli) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its horizontal interrupted range of presence extends across the African tropical rainforest (mainly West Africa, on either side of the Dahomey Gap). Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland.

children.name: Illadopsis albipectus
children.description: The scaly-breasted illadopsis (Illadopsis albipectus) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is widespread throughout the Congo Basin, with a few isolated pockets in northern Angola, Uganda and South Sudan. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, specifically in the understory and lower levels.

children.name: Illadopsis cleaveri
children.description: The blackcap illadopsis (Illadopsis cleaveri) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Illadopsis pyrrhoptera
children.description: The mountain illadopsis (Illadopsis pyrrhoptera) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Illadopsis rufescens
children.description: The rufous-winged illadopsis (Illadopsis rufescens) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Benin, Ivory Coast, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Senegal, Sierra Leone, and Togo. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Illadopsis distans
children.description: The Tanzanian illadopsis (Illadopsis distans) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Illadopsis turdina
children.description: The spotted thrush-babbler (Illadopsis turdina) also known as the thrush babbler, is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Sudan, and Zambia. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland.

children.name: Ptyrticus
children.description: A monotypic African genus of thrush-like babbler, found in the miombo woodlands of south-central Africa.

children.name: Graminicola
children.description: A genus of two species of long-tailed, grass-dwelling babblers found in South and Southeast Asian grasslands.

children.name: Graminicola bengalensis
children.description: The Indian grassbird (Graminicola bengalensis) is a passerine bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Graminicola striatus
children.description: The Chinese grassbird (Graminicola striatus) is a bird species in the family Pellorneidae.
